reviews.reason: withdraw (L36) floors shares=assets*TS/TA; any assets with assets*TS<TA burns 0 shares and balanceOf-=0 never underflows, so a shareless address takes assets. Confirmed. Corrections: each call yields at most ceil(TA/TS)-1 assets, so the drain is geometric and stops once TA<=TS (holders keep >=~1 wei/share, never 0). With TS=1 (post-inflation) one call takes all but 1 wei; with 1000e18 shares and 10% yield each call yields 1 wei (dust). The claimed follow-on to totalAssets==0 is unreachable via this route.

executed.what_it_shows: test_C01_zeroShareWithdraw: shareless actor removes >800e18 of 1000e18 donated assets from a 1000-share vault while holding 0 shares; test_C01_realisticDust: with 1000e18 shares at 1.1 rate the max zero-share withdraw is 1 wei and 2 wei underflows.

reviews.reason: Empty vault mints 1:1, totalAssets is raw balance (donatable), previewDeposit floors, deposit has no shares>0 check. Attacker deposits 1 wei, donates 100e18, victim's 100e18 deposit mints 0 shares, attacker redeems 1 share for everything. Note: because of C01, any third party can also take the donated surplus with 0-share withdraws, so the attacker is racing others, but the victim loses regardless.

executed.what_it_shows: Victim receives 0 shares; attacker ends with 201e18 (own 101e18 + victim's 100e18).

reviews.reason: stake() calls _updatePool not _updateUser; userRewardPerTokenPaid stays 0 for a new address, so earned() applies the whole rewardPerTokenStored to the new stake; claim() then checkpoints that inflated amount into rewards and pays it out. Top-ups are also back-credited to the last checkpoint.

executed.what_it_shows: A stakes for 1000s at 1e18/s (1000e18 emitted to A); B stakes just afterwards and immediately has earned==1000e18 and claims it, double-paying the emissions.

reviews.reason: setPair (L22-24) has no onlyOwner, although the modifier exists and is used on setOwner. price() trusts any contract's getReserves. A fake pair returning (1, 2^112-1) values 1 wei of collateral at ~5.2e33 debt units, so borrow() can take the whole debtToken balance. The only extra requirement is a nonzero collateral deposit. The griefing variant (a reverting pair blocks borrow and withdrawCollateral) is real, but anyone can call setPair again to reverse it, so it becomes a tug-of-war rather than a permanent freeze.
reviews.settling_test: Deploy FakePair{getReserves returns (1,2^112-1)}; attacker depositCollateral(1), setPair(fake), borrow(pool debtToken balance) succeeds; assert pool debtToken balance == 0.

reviews.reason: price = r1*1e18/r0 from spot reserves; sync() is public and token1 donations raise r1; borrow checks price in the same tx; no TWAP and no liquidation. The donated token1 stays in the pair and can be partly recovered with swap0For1. The attack profits when 0.75*C*D/r0 > D (minus what is recovered), which means the collateral C must be large relative to r0 (shallow pair), as stated.
reviews.settling_test: Seed pair (r0=r1=100e18), pool funded with 10000e18 debtToken; attacker deposits 200e18 collateral, transfers 1000e18 token1 to pair, sync(), borrows 0.75*200*11=1650e18, swaps token0 in to recover token1; assert attacker net token1 gain > token0 collateral market value.

reviews.reason: distribute requires every transfer to succeed; recipients and shares are fixed at construction; owner is unused; there is no rescue or pull path. Any recipient whose transfer reverts or returns false (blacklist, address(0) rejection, zero-amount revert with a 0-bps share, which the constructor allows) blocks all payouts permanently. Conditional on token behaviour or the deployer's configuration. The gas-limit case is chosen by the deployer, not an attacker.
reviews.settling_test: Mock token that reverts on transfer to a blacklisted address; construct splitter with that recipient; fund it; assert distribute() reverts and no other path moves funds.

reviews.reason: There is no liquidate/seize function anywhere in LendingPool; the LTV check runs only in borrow/withdrawCollateral of the acting user. swap0For1 (token0 in) lowers r1/r0, so the price can fall and leave positions underwater with no recourse. This is a design-level solvency gap.
reviews.settling_test: Borrow at 75% LTV, swap token0 into pair to halve price, assert debtOf > collateral value and no function lets a third party reduce the bad debt.

reviews.reason: The arithmetic is true (deposit and withdraw divide by totalAssets()==0 when totalSupply>0; redeem would pay 0). The stated route is not: C01 zero-share withdraws stop once TA<=TS (each call needs assets*TS<TA), and redeem of fewer than totalSupply shares floors below TA, so the vault's own functions can never reach TA==0 with TS>0. Only external token behaviour (negative rebase, seizure or blacklist of the vault) gets there. Low severity, and the 'follow-on of rounding bug' framing is wrong.

executed.what_it_shows: Partial redeem of 9 of 10 shares leaves 1 asset/1 share (TA>0); with test_C01 the zero-share drain terminates with TA>0.

reviews.settling_test: To confirm the residual case: mock token with an admin burnFrom(vault); burn the vault balance to 0 with shares outstanding; assert deposit reverts.

reviews.reason: When totalStaked==0, rewardPerToken returns stored while _updatePool still sets lastUpdate, so emissions are dropped. The increment floors per update, and stake(0) is callable by anyone (zero transferFrom succeeds on standard tokens), so updates can be forced. Full zeroing needs totalStaked > dt*rewardRate*1e18, which is only realistic with tiny rates, but per-update dust loss always occurs. No theft.
reviews.settling_test: rate=1, stake 2e18, warp 1s and call stake(0) repeatedly; assert rewardPerTokenStored unchanged after N seconds.

reviews.reason: swap0For1 treats balance-reserve0 as input with no caller binding, so a transfer and swap done in separate txs can be front-run or absorbed by sync(). That matches the 'transfer first' Uniswap-v2 pattern and is user error without a router. sync's uint112(...) is an explicit downcast, which truncates silently in 0.8 (no revert). That is real but needs >=2^112 units.
reviews.settling_test: Transfer token0 to pair from user, then a different address calls swap0For1 and receives the output; separately mint 2^112+1 token0 to pair, sync, assert reserve0==1.

reviews.reason: The push at L40 happens whenever debtOf==0 before the add. borrow(0) leaves debt at 0, so every call pushes again, and repay-then-reborrow pushes again. The array is never pruned. borrowerCount just returns the (inflated) length via a loop. Each inflation costs the attacker ~22k+ gas, and the view is only gas-bound for on-chain or eth_call caps. No funds at risk.
reviews.settling_test: Call borrow(0) 5 times from one address; assert borrowerCount()==5.

reviews.reason: (dt)*rewardRate*1e18 is checked. With rate > 2^256/1e18, every call with dt>=1 overflows. stake/withdraw/claim/setRewardRate all hit _updatePool first, there is no emergency withdraw, and totalStaked can't drop to 0 because withdraw reverts, so the freeze is permanent. Nuance: in the same block (dt==0) setRewardRate still succeeds, so the owner can only undo it within that block. Privileged-misconfiguration risk.

executed.what_it_shows: After setting rate=2^256/1e18+1 and warping 1s, setRewardRate(0), withdraw and claim all revert; the same-block reset succeeds.

reviews.reason: claim transfers the full accrued amount under require with no partial path. Accrual is not tied to funding, and C03 lets fresh stakers draw down the reserve, so later claimants revert. withdraw pays no rewards, so principal stays withdrawable. The root cause duplicates C03; on its own (underfunding) it is a liveness issue.
reviews.settling_test: Extend test_C03: fund only 1000e18 rewards; after B claims, assert A's claim reverts while A.withdraw succeeds.

reviews.reason: token1.transfer (L28) precedes sync() (L29) with no lock. A reentrant swap0For1 sees the same balance-reserve0 input and the stale reserves, so the k check passes again and amountOut is paid twice for one input. This only applies if token1 calls back into the recipient (ERC777-like); with a plain ERC20 there is no reentry.

executed.what_it_shows: With a hook-calling token1, one 100e18 token0 input yields 2x90e18 token1 (honest max ~90.9e18).

reviews.reason: LendingPool.depositCollateral/repay and RewardPool.stake credit the nominal amount, so with fee-on-transfer tokens they become insolvent for the last withdrawers. ShareVault is different: shares are pro-rata on the real balance (redeem uses totalAssets), so a fee-on-transfer depositor is over-minted, which dilutes existing holders. That is value transfer, not insolvency; the 'last withdrawers cannot exit' impact does not apply to ShareVault. Conditional on a non-standard token.
reviews.settling_test: 1% fee token: two users stake 100 each in RewardPool (pool receives 198); assert second withdraw(100) reverts.

reviews.reason: withdrawCollateral always calls price(), which divides by r0, so a debt-free user cannot withdraw while r0==0. Mitigating detail: reserves only update via the public sync/swap, and token0 can never leave the pair (swap0For1 only sends token1), so once the pair holds any token0, anyone can call sync() to restore r0>0. The freeze is temporary unless the pair is never seeded (or via the C04 setPair route or the impractical truncation). Low.
reviews.settling_test: Deploy pair unseeded; depositCollateral(10) with debt 0; assert withdrawCollateral(10) reverts with division by zero; then seed pair+sync and assert it succeeds.

notes: Tests are in <scratchpad>/specprobe/challenge-work/test/Challenge.t.sol (fixture copied to <scratchpad>/specprobe/challenge-work/src, unmodified); run with: cd <scratchpad>/specprobe/challenge-work && <scratchpad>/tools/forge test --offline . All 7 tests pass (each asserts the claimed property; C08's test shows the vault itself cannot reach TA==0). The main corrections are to C01 (geometric drain to TA~TS, not to 0; dust-only at typical share counts), C08 (unreachable via vault logic), C15 (ShareVault impact is dilution rather than insolvency), C04 (the griefing can be reversed by anyone) and C12 (the owner can undo the setting within the same block). C03/C13 share a root cause, as do C04/C05/C16 (price source).
